Legacy equipment is manually controlled and highly dependent on skilled operators. The CNC systems can accommodate closed-loop control with advanced sensors, which could reduce the skills required to operate the system, increase traceability, and enable advanced process development. Figure 26: Left) Manual controlled electron beam welding vs Right) CNC controlled electron beam welding [55, 56] Motion Control Inside of the Vacuum Chamber Motion inside vacuum is completed via electrical feedthrough to a linear or rotary motion system inside the chamber. Custom vacuum rated motors are needed to move the large loads (50-1500kg) over meters of stroke in electron beam welding of copper accelerators which estimated to have a mass of 650 lbs (300 kg). In addition to vacuum rating, these motors need to be EMF shielded so that they do not interfere and distort the electron beam. Considerations regarding motor cooling in vacuum as well as low-outgassing lubricants in the bearing and slides is needed.
